stories.title: How wildfires are scorching France’s wine industry
stories.summary: Europe’s largest wine exporter is already battling a cocktail of crisis from heatwaves to lower sales. As wildfires razed swaths of Western Europe this summer, wineries in the region have grown increasingly concerned about the fate of one of the area’s most important exports. In France, Europe’s largest wine exporter by far, some 739,000 hectares (1.8 million acres) of land is dedicated to vineyards that sprawl across wine-making regions such as Languedoc, Bordeaux and the Rhone Valley. So has it been for centuries. But now, human-induced climate change is causing more extreme weather conditions, threatening the precious and fragile grapes, which are particularly sensitive to heat. Worse, the frequency of wildfires in the tinder-dry forests is rising, causing havoc to agriculture. This year, Western Europe endured one of its hottest summers, aggravated by the El Nino weather phenomenon, which is characterised by hotter, drier conditions. Europe is now the planet’s fastest-warming continent, and in some places, is ill-equipped to deal with hot weather. This year’s hot season began with a suffocating heat dome in May, and by mid-August, punishing temperatures reached 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit) in some areas. Wildfires tore through areas of Gironde, southwestern France, close to Bordeaux and in the heart of wine country. Higher temperatures force grapes to ripen much faster than normal. While that produces a more sugary flavour, it also affects the grape’s natural acidity and pushes up alcohol content in the wine it produces.

stories.title: US may ‘review position’ on Malvinas Islands sovereignty, Trump says
stories.summary: British outlets report Washington is using the issue to threaten the UK to get it to increase defense spending on NATO La entrada US may ‘review position’ on Malvinas Islands sovereignty, Trump says se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald .
article_sentences: United States President Donald Trump said on Monday that he may “review” his country’s position on the sovereignty dispute over the Malvinas Islands between Argentina and the United Kingdom.

Until now the U.S. has not endorsed either Argentina’s or Britain’s claim to ultimate sovereignty over the archipelago, but Washington formally acknowledges that the UK administers the islands in practice.
The veiled comment followed reports published last week by British outlet.

The Telegraph that the U.S. had threatened to challenge British sovereignty over the islands if the UK failed to increase defense spending and contributions to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).
“I always review every position.
That’s just one of many,” Trump said after reporters asked him in the Oval Office whether the U.S. was reviewing its position on the Malvinas.
Reporters also asked whether he wanted the government of new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to increase its current NATO spending commitments.
“The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved,” Trump answered.

Prior reports by UK media indicated that Chancellor John Healey — who oversees the country’s economy and finance ministry — would delay Britain’s previous commitment to spend 3% of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) on defense by 2030.
Trump has pressured U.S. allies to increase their defense spending and NATO contributions and has accused them of “freeloading” on United States military resources.
At the 2025 NATO Summit in The Hague, member states committed to increasing total defense and security spending to 5% of GDP annually by 2035.

Reports of a potential review of the U.S. position on the Malvinas first emerged in April, although at the time the U.S. State Department told AFP news agency that it would “remain one of neutrality.”

stories.title: Napoli’s ex Man Utd star McTominay needs surgery for irregular heartbeat
stories.summary: Scotland international Scott McTominay, who joined Napoli from Manchester United, to undergo heart surgery. Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay will undergo a surgical procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat, the Serie. A club has announced. Napoli added that McTominay will be out until after the season’s first international break, meaning he won’t play again until October. “Following the development of a minor, benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay over the coming days will undergo an operation a PFA [pulsed field ablation],” Napoli said on Tuesday. A PFA is a minimally invasive technique used to treat heart arrhythmias. The 29-year-old was Serie A’s MVP when he helped Napoli win the title in 2025. He played for Scotland at this year’s World Cup and was also listed among the contenders for the last Ballon d’Or. McTominay exited during the second half of Napoli’s 2-1 loss to Como on Sunday. A product of the Manchester United youth system, which he joined during the Alex Ferguson tenure as manager of the Premier League club, McTominay has played in 73 internationals for Scotland, scoring 15 goals. His 2024 move to Napoli came after seven seasons in the United first team.
